text: What Isaac knows is not told in Genesis 22. He carries the wood; he asks about the lamb; he receives an answer which is no answer to the question. Of his inward thought or feeling the narrator gives nothing, recording only that they went, both of them, together. The phrase recurs, and repetition is put in the place of explanation. The question of Isaac’s consent is raised and set aside unresolved; the logic of Obedience settles everything, and leaves nothing unaccounted for.
